newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber market steady, China buys.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber market steady, China buys.

text.p: Singapore rubber market prices were steady by midday on Tuesday with China said to have bought several hundred tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber over the past few days, dealers said.
"We heard the Chinese bought some cargoes of RSS3 as they were attracted by the low level of prices they were seeing. But I think the buying has slowed down a bit today," a trader said.

Traders said there was also some modest shortcovering in the morning session for RSS1 grade rubber while other buyers held off on expectations that prices will still come off. "People feel lower prices are still in the offing," one said.

The trade also felt that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) will not intervene in the market soon since prices were only approaching "may-buy" levels while the "must-buy" mark has not yet been threatened.
"Most people don't believe INRO will come in now. The 'must-buy' level is still about 10 (Malaysian/Singapore) cents away," a dealer said.

At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 88.50-90.50 U.S. cents a kg from 91.00 cents. August RSS1 was seen at 132.00-134.00 Singapore cents (92-93 U.S. cents) a kg from 134.25 cents. - (US$1 = S$1.43) - Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
